extracted.intended_audience: marketers, product teams, founders and anyone trying to get a story onto Hacker News
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidelines for when and how to submit links to Hacker News to maximize chances of landing the front page, including timing, title crafting, relevance, submission/linking mechanics, and upvoting tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit at 8:00 AM EST
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit at 8:00 AM EST. If you miss the window (after 8:20 AM), simply post the day or week after.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specific time window is recommended for scheduling; missing the early window means waiting to avoid worse visibility. The author notes this was assembled 18 months prior and practices may have changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferably on Wednesday
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wednesdays seem to be the peak of traffic for HN (more eyeballs). The author also notes weekends' front page may be easier to land (example), but Wednesday gives peak traffic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have a great title
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a great title: relevant and catchy, use capitalization and potentially use slang.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples / tips: capitalization helps; using slang (the post specifically mentions a simple “sh*t” in the title) can increase attention. A great title attracts clicks and upvotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be opinionated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having a strong opinion helps create discussion and buzz among readers, which generates upvotes and visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be relevant to HN audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Be relevant: HN is a community of hackers and entrepreneurs, so post about entrepreneurship, technology or the related lifestyle and interests of such people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content outside those topical areas is less likely to resonate and get upvoted.

rubrics_metrics.name: One upvote per IP address (voting limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: One upvote per IP address; votes from the same IP (e.g., office) won’t be taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: if multiple team members vote from the same IP, only one counts — submit the story from a different IP and ensure upvoters use distinct connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit the story from a different IP
rubrics_metrics.description: You need to submit the story from a different IP (so team/office IP collisions don't suppress votes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine this with using separate connections for upvoting (mobile phone or home) to avoid multiple votes coming from the same IP and being ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct links to the post don’t allow people to vote
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct links to the post (e.g., item?id=...) won’t work for upvoting; people must vote from the newest page or the front page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asking others to upvote, share the newest page (http://news.ycombinator.com/newest) right after submission, and later update to the front page link if the story reaches the front page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put the name and the direct URL (no URL shortener)
rubrics_metrics.description: Put the name and the direct URL when submitting; do not use URL shorteners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full direct URL to the content to avoid issues or distrust caused by shortened links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share the newest page link immediately and ask for upvotes
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as submitted, share the newest page link on Twitter, GTalk, IM and ask friends for an upvote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to generate early, fast upvotes which HN values. Note the author’s edit: after experimentation they may not recommend coordinated asking because HN may detect voting rings and penalize repeated friend upvoting.

rubrics_metrics.name: If the story reaches the front page, update to front page link
rubrics_metrics.description: If you get on the front page, update the shared link to the front page link (http://news.ycombinator.com/).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Switching to the front page link makes it easier for visitors to find and vote on the story from the front page context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use separate internet connections for team upvoting
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure team members use separate connections if they upvote the post (use mobile phones or vote from home).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces the chance multiple upvotes are ignored for coming from the same IP address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed of early upvotes matters
rubrics_metrics.description: HN mainly cares about the speed at which you collect upvotes, not who you are or where the post comes from.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collecting votes quickly after submission increases chances to reach the front page and to snowball; fewer votes may be needed depending on front-page competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect a temporary traffic boost (conversion may be poor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Being on the front page can bring tens of thousands of visitors in a single day, but this boost is temporary and may convert poorly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage expectations: front-page traffic often fades quickly and may not lead to sustained engagement or conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing fallback: miss window -> post later
rubrics_metrics.description: If you miss the early submission window (after ~8:20 AM EST), don’t try later the same morning; post the day or week after.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This repeats the timing rule and advises against late-morning submissions that likely have poorer visibility.
